title: Specified etale sum base change is the pullback mate and preserves evaluation
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $e:U\to X$ be separated etale of finite type, and let $w:X'\to X$ be any morphism between Noetherian schemes; Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Form the Cartesian square with $U'=U\times_XX'$, $e':U'\to X'$ and $w':U'\to U$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Work with constant-$A$ module sheaves on the ordinary small etale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. On sheaves put $H=w^*$, $J=w'^*$, $L=e_{\Sigma!}$, $L'=e'_{\Sigma!}$, $R=e^*$, $R'=e'^*$, using sum extension [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], its sum/restriction adjunction [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], and exact inverse image with its direct-image adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Write $u:\mathrm{id}\to RL$, $v:LR\to\mathrm{id}$ and $v':L'R'\to\mathrm{id}$ for these sum unit and counits, and $\chi:JR\xrightarrow{\sim}R'H$ for the canonical pullback-composition comparison.

Let $\beta:L'J\to HL$ be the specified sheaf comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]: its conjugate for the composite adjunctions $HL\dashv RH_*$ and $L'J\dashv J_*R'$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] is the module-linear ordinary exchange $\operatorname{Ex}^0:RH_*\to J_*R'$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear]. This specified transformation is the inverse mate of $\chi$ for $L\dashv R$ and $L'\dashv R'$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]; explicitly,
$$\beta_M=v'_{HLM}\circ L'(\chi_{LM})\circ L'J(u_M).$$
For every module sheaf $N$ on $X$ it satisfies
$$H(v_N)\circ\beta_{RN}=v'_{HN}\circ L'(\chi_N).$$
The isomorphism $b^\Sigma: w^*S_e\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{e'}w'^*$, where $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})$, is the degreewise inverse of this same $\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules]. For every $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$w^*\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ(b^\Sigma_{e^*K})^{-1}=\operatorname{ev}_{e',w^*K}\circ S_{e'}(\chi_K).$$
Here $\chi_K:w'^*e^*K\to e'^*w^*K$ is the derived pullback identification, and $\operatorname{ev}$ denotes the sum/evaluation counit. At $K=A_X$ the canonical constant-sheaf pullback identifications identify $\chi_{A_X}$ with the identity of $A_{U'}$.

proof.text: Put a and a′ equal to the published sum/restriction adjunctions, b and b′ equal to the inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions for w′ and w, and chi equal to squareUpperStarIso. Apply injectivity of conjugateEquiv for a.comp b′ and b.comp a′. Expand the definition of etaleLowerShriekBaseChangeMap; iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and the two inverse laws identify its conjugate with the mate defining baseChangeMap. Thus the specified sheaf map is exactly the inverse mate of chi.
Expand the inverse-mate definition at M to obtain its unit/comparison/counit component formula. Apply mateEquiv_counit_symm to chi and reverse the equality to obtain the sheaf counit formula at N.

Unfold exactEtaleSumExchange and mapDerivedCategorySquareIso. The identity mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_symm and associativity identify the former with the inverse of the derived square of asIso beta. Invertibility of beta is the published etale lower-shriek base-change theorem.

Use exact_localization_inverse_mate for a, a′ and chi. The two exactLocalizationDerivedAdjunction constructions are definitionally the published derivedEtaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction constructions, both obtained by localizing the same termwise adjunction with the same exact-functor factorizations. The theorem identifies the inverse mate of D(chi) with the derived square of asIso beta. Apply mateEquiv_counit_symm at an arbitrary unbounded derived object K and substitute the derived-square normalization from the preceding step. This is the asserted derived evaluation identity.

Apply the fully proved etaleSumExchangeConstantSquare with the same A, e and w. Its canonical constant comparison is the unchanged etaleSumExchangeConstantIso, now isolated in EtaleSumExchangeConstantIso. The theorem supplies exactly the final conjunct; its proof is the sheaf constant-composition coherence transported by the exact-single API.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03S6; categories.tex Tags 0B65 and 0DV0; derived.tex Tag 015F. Formal route uses the proved exact-localization inverse-mate theorem and source exact-single and constant-composition coherence lemmas.
